label: COVID-19 market crash
description: S&P 500 fell 34% in 33 days. Fed cut rates to zero, launched unlimited QE.

label: Fed tightening cycle 2022
description: Fed began fastest rate hike cycle since 1980s. 525bps over 16 months.

label: SVB collapse
description: Silicon Valley Bank failed due to HTM bond losses. Triggered regional bank contagion fears.

label: Russia invades Ukraine
description: Commodity shock. WTI surged to $130. European energy crisis. USD safe-haven bid.

label: US-China trade war begins
description: Trump announced tariffs on $50B of Chinese goods. Escalated through 2019.

label: Fed 25bp Rate Cut – Dec 2024
description: The Federal Reserve cut the fed funds rate by 25 basis points to 4.25–4.50%, citing cooling inflation and rising unemployment. The decision triggered immediate weakness in the dollar and a rally in gold.

label: Iran Direct Attack on Israel – Apr 2024
description: Iran launched over 300 drones and ballistic missiles directly at Israel in the first-ever direct military confrontation between the two nations, with over 99% intercepted. Markets spiked on fears of broader Middle East escalation before partially recovering as the limited scope of retaliation became clear.

label: Crypto Selloff on Fed Higher-for-Longer – Apr 2024
description: Bitcoin fell 15% in a week after the Federal Reserve signalled rates would remain higher for longer, with Ethereum and crypto-related equities declining in tandem. The selloff reflected crypto's increasing correlation with high-beta risk assets and sensitivity to real yield movements.

label: US-Iran Framework Deal Announced – Jun 2026
description: President Trump announced a framework agreement with Iran to end their months-long war, calling off planned US strikes and signalling the Strait of Hormuz would reopen once finalized; oil prices fell sharply across two sessions to multi-month lows despite Tehran publicly disputing the deal's terms.

label: US Equities Surge as Trump Cancels Iran Strikes
description: US equities staged a sharp rally (S&P 500 +1.7-1.8%, Nasdaq +2.5%, Dow +930pts) and the VIX fell nearly 12% after Trump cancelled planned strikes on Iran and signalled a peace deal was imminent. Falling oil prices pulled Treasury yields lower, high-beta tech led gains, while energy, real estate and utilities declined.

label: Draft US-Iran MOU Details Reported (Sanctions Relief, Hormuz)
description: Iran's state-run Mehr News Agency reported details of a draft 14-point memorandum of understanding between the US and Iran, including US lifting of oil sanctions on Iran, mutual reopening of Strait of Hormuz transit, and an end to regional hostilities including Lebanon. Oil extended its decline while Treasury yields edged higher after Thursday's sharp drop, and global equities (Stoxx 600, Nikkei, Kospi) rallied further.

label: US-Iran Peace Deal Confirmed – Hormuz Naval Blockade Ends
description: Pakistan's PM and President Trump confirmed a final peace deal between the US and Iran ending the nearly four-month war, with both sides declaring immediate and permanent termination of hostilities on all fronts including Lebanon, and Trump announcing the end of the US naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. WTI fell further toward $85 while global equities extended their rally and gold declined as the geopolitical risk premium collapsed; formal signing ceremony was scheduled for June 19 in Switzerland.

label: Nvidia $25B Bond Sale – AI Debt Financing Wave
description: Nvidia priced a $25 billion investment-grade bond offering across seven tranches (its first since 2021), attracting $85 billion in orders, as part of a broader wave of AI-infrastructure debt financing by hyperscalers expected to exceed $725 billion in capex in 2026. The deal, led by Goldman Sachs, JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley, signalled that the AI buildout is now being financed as much through fixed income as through equity markets.

label: Bank of Japan Hikes to 1% – 30-Year High
description: The Bank of Japan raised its policy rate by 25bp to 1.0% in a 7-1 vote, the highest level since 1995, citing Iran-war-driven energy inflation pushing core CPI toward and above the 2% target and a persistently weak yen requiring structural support beyond FX intervention. May trade data released June 17 showed exports up 17% YoY (chip shipments +61.2%) but a widening trade deficit as yen-inflated imports grew 12.5%, with the Nikkei rising on the decision while USD/JPY remained near 160 as the widely-telegraphed hike failed to durably strengthen the yen.

label: Intel 18A-P Risk Production Begins – Apple Foundry Deal Advances
description: Intel announced 18A-P, its most advanced chip process node, has entered risk production, bringing it closer to securing Apple as a foundry customer and validating Intel's foundry turnaround under CEO Lip-Bu Tan. Intel shares have risen over 200% YTD, underpinned by a 10% US government equity stake, a $5B Nvidia investment, and Microsoft and Amazon foundry commitments, with CEO Tan expecting multiple foundry customer commitments in H2 2026.

label: Warsh's First FOMC: Hold, Hawkish Dot Plot, Drop Forward Guidance
description: New Fed Chair Kevin Warsh held rates steady at 3.50–3.75% at his first FOMC meeting, but the dot plot flipped hawkish with a 9-9 split and median dot pointing to a 25bp hike later in 2026 — a reversal from March's projection of a cut — as CPI hit 4.2% YoY (a 3-year high) driven by the Iran-war energy spike. Warsh dropped the Fed's forward guidance framework entirely, slashed the post-meeting statement to 130 words, and launched task forces to review communications, the balance sheet, and inflation frameworks; markets sold off sharply on the hawkish shift.

label: Vance Defends Iran MOU; Gas Below $4; Republican Backlash
description: VP Vance held a White House press conference defending the signed US-Iran MOU, confirming Iran receives no direct US payments and that all economic benefits (sanctions relief, $300B reconstruction fund access, frozen asset unfreezing) are compliance-contingent; simultaneously gas prices fell below $4/gallon nationally for the first time since the war began as oil markets priced in Hormuz reopening, while Republican Senate backlash threatened Congressional ratification of the deal's sanctions-relief provisions.

label: Trump Confirms Apple-Intel US Chip Deal via Truth Social
description: President Trump announced via Truth Social that Apple agreed to work with Intel to design and build chips in America, sending Intel shares up over 10% to an all-time high. Apple will reportedly use Intel's 18A-P process for lower-end chips (non-Pro iPhones, older iPad/MacBook models) only, with TSMC retaining over 90% of Apple's leading-edge silicon supply amid capacity constraints from AI chipmaker demand.

label: Global AI/Chip Tech Selloff — KOSPI -10%, Nasdaq -2.2%
description: A valuation-driven global selloff in AI and semiconductor stocks saw Samsung and SK Hynix plunge >12%, triggering double circuit breakers in South Korea and dragging the KOSPI down 10%. The Nasdaq fell 2.2%, QQQ dropped >3%, and European tech indices shed 1-3%, with no single catalyst but broad investor anxiety around AI capex ROI sustainability and pre-Micron earnings nervousness.

label: US Treasury General License X — 60-Day Iran Oil Sanctions Waiver
description: The US Treasury OFAC issued General License X on June 22, authorising the production, sale, dollar-denominated payment, and import of Iranian crude oil and petrochemicals through August 21, 2026 — the most sweeping rollback of Iran oil sanctions since 1979 — unlocking ~67 million barrels of stranded Gulf inventory and sending WTI down 2.7% to $73.82 and Brent down 2.8% to $78.29. The waiver covers the full commercial stack (banking, insurance, shipping, vessel management) and is tied to Iran's Strait of Hormuz transit commitments under the June 17 MOU.

label: Ghalibaf Rejects US Ag Claim; Cargo Ship Hit at Hormuz
description: Iranian Parliament Speaker and chief negotiator Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf publicly repudiated Trump's assertion that $12B in unfrozen Iranian assets would be used to buy US agricultural goods, calling the claim 'false' and exposing a fundamental implementation rift in the MOU; simultaneously, a cargo ship transiting the Strait of Hormuz on a UN-backed route was struck by a projectile (attributed by a US official to Iran), prompting the IMO to pause its ship evacuation programme and the IRGC to warn all vessels using the alternative non-Iranian-approved route.

label: June 25 Market Day: Micron Blowout, PCE In-Line, Fed Stress Test Pass, Apple Price Hikes
description: Four simultaneous market-moving events shaped trading on June 25: Micron surged 17% on blowout Q3 results ($25.11 EPS vs $20.78 est, $50B Q4 revenue guide) validating the AI/HBM demand cycle; May PCE came in at 4.1% YoY / 3.4% core (highest since Oct 2023, but in-line), relieving fears of an upside inflation shock; all 32 major US banks passed the Fed's 2026 stress test with no capital buffer changes, triggering immediate dividend hikes at JPM (+10%), GS (+11%), and MS (+15%); and Apple fell 6% after announcing 15-25% price hikes on MacBooks and iPads, explicitly blaming the AI-driven memory cost surge — transmitting HBM market tightness directly into consumer electronics prices and CPI.

label: UK-France-Oman Hormuz Security Pact; France Deploys Minehunters
description: UK PM Starmer and French President Macron issued a joint statement on July 3 announcing Oman's agreement to work with the UK and France to ensure safe navigation through its sovereign territorial waters adjacent to the Strait of Hormuz, with both nations standing ready to deploy a wider Multinational Military Mission; France simultaneously confirmed deployment of two minehunters, two frigates and a maritime patrol aircraft to the region while recalling the Charles de Gaulle carrier. The agreement formalises the Omani-corridor route as the Western-backed alternative to Iranian-controlled lanes, directly contesting IRGC sovereignty claims over Hormuz transit — and comes against a backdrop of resumed ceasefire fragility including IRGC strikes on Kuwait and Bahrain (June 28), brief Hormuz re-closure, Doha technical talks, and Ghalibaf's confirmation that Iran has exported 40 million barrels post-MOU at a 20% price premium.

label: Trump Reinstates Iran Blockade; MOU Collapses; Oil +9.4%, Yields +6bps
description: Following a weekend of mutual heavy airstrikes (US hitting 140+ Iranian military targets Saturday, IRGC hitting US bases in Jordan, Kuwait, Bahrain and Oman on Sunday), President Trump announced via Truth Social on July 13 that the US was reinstating a naval blockade on Iranian ports — effectively declaring the June 17 MOU dead — and simultaneously claimed a 20% toll on all cargo transiting Hormuz for US protection services; WTI surged 9.4% to $78.14 (largest daily gain since 2020), Brent rose 9.6% to $83.30, the S&P 500 fell 0.79%, Nasdaq fell 1.55%, Treasury yields rose 4-6 basis points (10Y to 4.614%), and markets immediately repriced to at least one Fed rate hike by year-end, with June CPI and Warsh's first Congressional testimony both due Tuesday.

label: Trump Threatens Canada Tariff Hike Over Wildfire Smoke; USMCA Sunset Triggered
description: President Trump posted on Truth Social on July 17 holding Canada responsible for wildfire smoke from 896 active blazes blanketing 18 US states and DC (100M+ people under air quality alerts), threatening to add the 'cost of this pollution' to existing Canadian tariffs — framed as 'willful negligence' in forest management; the threat comes with compounding structural context: the Trump administration declined to renew USMCA earlier in July triggering a 10-year sunset period, and one intelligence source cited a tariff increase to 35% on nearly all Canadian goods, hammering the Canadian dollar to a two-year low and hitting lumber, autos, and auto parts with acute pain.

label: USTR Section 301: 25% Tariff on Brazil Effective July 22; Retaliation Threatened
description: USTR Greer concluded a yearlong Section 301 investigation on July 16, imposing a 25% tariff on most Brazilian imports (effective July 22), targeting six practice areas: digital trade/electronic payments, unfair preferential tariffs to Mexico and India, anti-corruption enforcement, IP protection, ethanol market access, and illegal deforestation; a separate forced-labour probe due the following week could add a further 12.5% for a potential 37.5% total burden — Brazil immediately vowed retaliation under its Reciprocity Law, with options including curbs on US audiovisual companies, suspension of pharmaceutical and agricultural patents, and WTO dispute settlement, while BRL weakened sharply and Brazil's October 2026 presidential election created domestic political complication for Lula.

label: Hormuz Traffic Collapses to 8 Transits/Day; 9 Ships Attacked; Red Sea Threat Emerges
description: By July 17, Hormuz transit traffic had collapsed to 8 vessels per day (down from 100+ pre-war and 37 just one week prior), with 9 ships attacked since July 6 as Iran forces vessels onto its northern territorial route rather than the US-protected Omani corridor; General License X was revoked by OFAC on July 8 reimposing Iran oil sanctions; maritime risk CEO cited 'worst case scenario' conditions including crews switching off AIS transponders, GPS spoofing intensifying, and no LNG tankers visible on tracking systems — while Iran and Houthi allies in Yemen threatened to extend the shutdown to the Red Sea, threatening to close the last major alternative oil export route for Saudi Arabia.

label: CNBC Analysis: Iran's Fragmented Power Structure Structurally Undermines Ceasefire
description: A CNBC analytical piece draws on Chatham House and FDD expert testimony to formalise the structural explanation for why every Iran ceasefire has collapsed: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (son of Ali Khamenei, killed Feb 28) holds ultimate authority but does not direct tactical operations; President Pezeshkian shapes diplomacy but cannot command the armed forces; the IRGC exercises significant operational autonomy over missiles, drones, maritime interdiction, and regional proxy networks, answering directly to the Supreme Leader — creating a principal-agent problem where diplomatic agreements are undermined by IRGC commanders who have no incentive to comply and a new Supreme Leader whose grip on the IRGC is contested, with reports of the IRGC blocking Pezeshkian's presidential appointments and erecting a security cordon around Mojtaba Khamenei himself.

label: 30Y Treasury Hits 5.31% (19-Year High); FOMC Minutes Signal 9-3 Hold with Hawkish Shift; Retail Earnings Week
description: The 30-year Treasury yield surged to 5.31% — its highest level since 2007 — as markets priced in persistent oil-driven inflation and an increasingly hawkish Fed, with the July 28-29 FOMC minutes (released Wednesday August 19) confirming a 9-3 vote to hold at 3.5-3.75% with Hammack, Kashkari, and Logan dissenting for a 25bp hike (the first three-way same-direction dissent since September 2016), Chair Warsh discussing reducing the annual meeting schedule from 8 to 6, the Treasury Department separately announcing stepped-up purchases of longer-dated debt to provide relief to the long end; WTI settled near $84.94, Trump confirmed no Iran talks are scheduled and the naval blockade remains in full effect, chip stocks were the primary S&P drag (Western Digital -7%, Sandisk -9%, Marvell -8%, Seagate -9%), and retail earnings week (Walmart, Home Depot, Lowe's, Target) served as the consumer spending catalyst watch.

label: Nvidia Acquires Hugging Face $12.9B; Q2 Revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY); $108B Q3 Guide
description: Nvidia officially confirmed its $12.9 billion acquisition of open-source AI platform Hugging Face on September 4 — its second-largest deal after the $20B Groq asset purchase — on the same week it reported blowout Q2 FY2027 revenue of $96.22 billion (+106% YoY, $89B data centre), guided Q3 to $108 billion (supply-constrained, not demand-constrained), and forecasted 70% FY2028 growth; NVDA rose ~1.8% on the Hugging Face announcement as investors read the software ecosystem move as defensive positioning against hyperscaler custom ASIC competition (Microsoft, Google, Meta, Amazon), while CEO Jensen Huang explicitly pushed back on 'circular financing' comparisons to dot-com vendor lending and Huang stated demand is 'running meaningfully higher' than the supply-constrained guidance.

label: Vance Demands Fed Rate Cut ('Would Be Nice to Have Help'); Waller Signals Hold; 10Y at 4.76%
description: Vice President JD Vance publicly called on the Federal Reserve to cut interest rates at a White House press briefing on September 3, framing the demand around housing affordability — 'it would be nice to have some help from the Federal Reserve' — directly contradicting Fed Chair Warsh's recent signal of a possible rate hike to address persistent inflation; on the same day, Fed Governor Christopher Waller separately signalled he was 'inclined to support holding' rates at the September 16-17 FOMC meeting if disinflation trends continued (CPI due September 11 as the knife-edge data point), causing Treasury yields to fall across the curve with the 10Y at 4.76% (near a 3-year high) and the 30Y hovering near its 2007 high, while Treasury Secretary Bessent made parallel comments at G20 characterising the bond market as stable despite yields being 18bps higher than Trump's inauguration.

label: August NFP +162K (3x Estimate); Trump: 'Lower Rate or I Stop Trade With Deficit Countries'; 2Y Spikes to 19-Month High
description: August nonfarm payrolls printed 162,000 (nearly triple the 55,000 consensus), with July revised from -23,000 to +21,000 (+55,000 combined revisions), unemployment unchanged at 4.1%, and labour force participation rising from 61.4% to 61.6% — the strongest jobs report in five months; Trump responded via Truth Social within 90 minutes demanding the Fed cut rates ('Lower the rate or I'll stop trading with countries with which we have a deficit'), threatening to weaponise trade policy against deficit-running trading partners as a coercive lever on the Federal Reserve, causing the 2-year Treasury yield to spike to a 19-month high of 4.4% and CME FedWatch to price a September rate hike at 60% probability, before Trump's own trade threat comments partially rallied Treasuries as markets re-priced the growth/trade-disruption risk of the ultimatum.

label: Fed Hikes 25bp Unanimously to 3.75–4.00%; Dot Plot Signals One More 2026 Hike; WTI >$100
description: The Federal Reserve unanimously voted to raise the federal funds rate 25 basis points to 3.75%–4.00% — the first hike since July 2023 — with Chair Warsh framing it as removing 'a dose of accommodation' to achieve a 'timelier return' to 2% inflation; the updated dot plot showed 12 of 18 officials projecting one additional 25bp hike by year-end (to 4.125%), four officials projecting 4.375%, and 2027 rate cuts removed entirely, while Warsh explicitly stated 'this summer's inflation readings do not tell me that underlying trends have meaningfully improved' and acknowledged the Strait of Hormuz oil shock is not something the Fed can address with rate policy, all while refusing to confirm or deny recent contact with President Trump — with WTI above $100 and the 2-year yield climbing to its highest level since 2024.

label: Trump Blames 'Hostile Board' for Hike; Rates Should Be '1% or Less'; White House Calls Hike 'Unfortunate'; Markets Applaud Credibility
description: Within hours of the unanimous Fed rate hike, Trump posted on Truth Social demanding rates of '1% or less' and publicly characterised the hike as the product of a 'hostile board' that Chair Warsh 'couldn't overpower' — explicitly separating Warsh from the decision to protect their political relationship while blaming unnamed board members, with the White House formally calling the hike an 'unfortunate decision'; simultaneously, markets applauded the hike from a credibility perspective (DXY surged 0.65%, stocks little-changed, Dow later fell 650 points on Warsh's hawkish remarks), and Trump repeated his '1% or less' demand at a North Carolina rally in the evening — creating a new political dynamic in which Trump attempts to maintain a personal alliance with Warsh while delegitimising the FOMC board as a whole.

label: Democrats Sweep 2026 Midterms: House 250+, Senate 54 Seats; Dow +1,524pts; Iran War Cited as Key Driver of GOP Defeat
description: Democrats swept the 2026 midterm elections on November 4, flipping the House (250+ seats, largest majority since 2008) and Senate (54 seats, 7 flipped), ending the Republican trifecta for Trump's final two years — the most decisive midterm repudiation since 2010, with exit polls showing voters who rated the economy as 'bad' and cited inflation as a hardship voted overwhelmingly Democrat, and Trump himself acknowledging the Iran war played a role in the defeat; markets surged on November 4 (Dow +1,524pts/+2.9%, S&P +1.8%, Nasdaq +2.1%) on a 'gridlock dividend' thesis — with Brent oil falling on Iran war de-escalation expectations, defense stocks retreating, Tesla and SpaceX falling 4-5%, and AI/data centre stocks under initial pressure on Democratic AI infrastructure scrutiny fears before recovering.
